note: The PoC obtains a live DOMAttr wrapper from an existing document, so the wrapper already points at a libxml attribute node.
A second DOMAttr object is created through the constructor path that frees any prior node stored in the wrapper.
The newly constructed attribute is attached to an element, exercising attribute ownership transfer and wrapper bookkeeping.
The constructor receives attacker-controlled strings from the script.
A new libxml attribute node is allocated from the supplied strings.
The wrapper's previous node pointer is fetched before replacement.
The previous node is freed here; the vulnerability hypothesis is that stale wrapper state can make this free unsafe.
The wrapper is updated after the free, so the free is the memory-safety sink in this path.
